mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates growing demand and economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with sustained 3-month increases in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a contraction in supply, leading to reduced corporate output and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between rising consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) and falling real personal savings (RSAFS) indicates reduced consumer purchasing power, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month AND RSAFS decrease > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL increases and RSAFS decreases as specified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of periods with sustained 3-month increases in PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a decreasing GDP (GDPC1) indicates a tightening monetary policy with a slowing economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increase > 0.5% in 1 month AND GDPC1 decrease > 0.5% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases and GDPC1 decreases as specified.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a quarter signals a significant contraction in supply, which leads to reduced corporate output and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially in a regime of high inflation.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 2% in a quarter during high inflation.
